title: Topology of an algebraic-space fibre over a scheme point
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be its structure map. For $t\in T$, form $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ using the residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the sheaf fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give point spaces their atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The projection $|X_t|\to |X|$ is a homeomorphism onto $|f|^{-1}(\{t\})$ with its subspace topology. In particular, the connectedness and nonemptiness of the fibre space can be read on this point inverse image. No separation, quasi-compactness, finite type, or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, $T$, or $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AC8, lemma-topology-fibre, for the quasi-compact residue-field monomorphism Spec kappa(t) -> T with T a scheme.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ with $U$ a scheme. Write $V=|f|^{-1}(\{t\})$ and $U_t=U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $U_t$ with $U\times_X X_t$: on every test scheme, both describe a map to $U$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ with the same composite to $T$. Pulling back $p$ gives a representable surjective etale atlas $q:U_t\to X_t$. The point maps of $p$ and $q$ are continuous, open and surjective. The scheme-fibre theorem identifies $|U_t|$ with $|p|^{-1}(V)\subseteq |U|$ with the induced topology, compatibly with the projections.

source.place: Tag 0AC8, lemma-topology-fibre, atlas diagram with Y=T, V=T, v=t; scheme input Tag 01K1 (schemes.tex, lemma-fibre-topological).

proof.text: Let $r:|X_t|\to V$ be induced by projection. Its image is all of $V$: the fibre-product point-image formula applied to $X\to T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, whose image is $\{t\}$, gives precisely this equality. For injectivity, take two field-valued representatives in $X_t$ with the same image class in $X$. By the definition of point classes their $X$-components agree after passage to a common field $M$, compatibly over $T$. Their two maps $\operatorname{Spec}M\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ have the same composite to $T$. The classification of maps from a field spectrum into the scheme $T$ says each must be the map induced by this composite on residue fields; hence these maps agree. The pairs therefore agree in the sheaf fibre product over $M$, so the original representatives give the same class in $|X_t|$. Thus $r$ is bijective. The projection is continuous by point-open calculus, and hence so is its corestriction to the subspace $V$.

source.place: Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian; Tag 03BU, definition-points; schemes.tex Tag 01J9, lemma-characterize-points and its preceding field-map classification. Tag 0AC8 uses the corresponding monomorphism argument.

proof.text: We now check openness explicitly in the atlas diagram, as in Tag 0AC8. If $A\subseteq |X_t|$ is open, $|q|^{-1}(A)$ is open in $|U_t|$. By step 1 there is an open $O\subseteq |U|$ such that this subset, viewed in $|U|$, equals $O\cap |p|^{-1}(V)$. Commutativity and the bijectivity in step 2 give $|q|^{-1}(A)=|p|^{-1}(r(A))$ under this identification. Surjectivity of $q$ now gives $r(A)=|p|(O\cap |p|^{-1}(V))=|p|(O)\cap V$. Since $p$ is open, this is open in $V$. Therefore the continuous bijection $r$ is open and its inverse is continuous, giving the asserted homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AC8, lemma-topology-fibre, the open-surjective atlas argument; here the target is already the scheme T, so no etale neighbourhood of the target is required.

proof.text: A bijection identifies nonemptiness in either direction. A homeomorphism also identifies decompositions into two disjoint nonempty open subsets, by taking images or inverse images. Thus $|X_t|$ is connected exactly when $V$ is connected, and nonempty exactly when $V$ is nonempty. This includes an empty fibre (with either space empty), a generic point $t$ which need not be locally closed, and a non-quasi-compact atlas; no finiteness or separation assumption was used.

lean.statement: theorem schemeFibre_point_homeomorphism {T : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace T) (t : T) : ∃ e : Point (X.obj.obj ⨯ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (T.fromSpecResidueField t))) ≃ₜ {x : Point X.obj.obj | ∃ p : PointRepresentative X.obj.obj, Quot.mk _ p = x ∧ p.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.K) = t}, (∀ p : PointRepresentative (X.obj.obj ⨯ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (T.fromSpecResidueField t))), (e (Quot.mk _ p)).val = Quot.mk _ (p.map (prod.fst (X := X.obj.obj) (Y := yoneda.obj (Over.mk (T.fromSpecResidueField t)))))) ∧ (PreconnectedSpace (Point (X.obj.obj ⨯ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (T.fromSpecResidueField t)))) ↔ PreconnectedSpace {x : Point X.obj.obj | ∃ p : PointRepresentative X.obj.obj, Quot.mk _ p = x ∧ p.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.K) = t}) ∧ (Nonempty (Point (X.obj.obj ⨯ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (T.fromSpecResidueField t)))) ↔ Nonempty {x : Point X.obj.obj | ∃ p : PointRepresentative X.obj.obj, Quot.mk _ p = x ∧ p.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.K) = t})
lean.note: Uses the presheaf product over T: on Sch/T the sheaf h_T is terminal, so this product is X ×_T h_{Spec κ(t)}, and products of sheaves are computed in presheaves. The representative equation specifies the canonical projection, rather than an arbitrary homeomorphism. The inverse-image subset is expanded by its field-valued representatives; its subtype carries the subspace topology. The final two clauses state preconnectedness and nonemptiness equivalences, which also imply ConnectedSpace equivalence.
